issues.sym: Slow starts, rough idle, misfires, or a fuel smell.
issues.why: The central injector unit's nozzles can gum up or leak as the truck ages.
issues.next: Have a shop test it. Treat any fuel smell as urgent.

issues.sym: Engine revs climb without acceleration, a gear goes missing, or reverse fails.
issues.why: The 4L60-E's 3-4 clutch pack is a known weak spot, especially in heavy SUVs that tow.
issues.next: Get a fluid check and road test soon. Stop towing until it is diagnosed.

issues.sym: Cracks appear across the top of the dash.
issues.why: Sun and heat break down the dash surface over time.
issues.next: Cosmetic. A dash cover helps. Keep cracks away from the air bag area in mind.

issues.sym: Frequent oil top-offs, low-oil message, blue smoke on startup, misfires.
issues.why: Oil passes the piston rings and burns, a problem tied to this engine family and its cylinder deactivation.
issues.next: Watch the dipstick closely and ask a GMC dealer for an oil consumption test.

issues.t: Lifter failure on V8s with cylinder deactivation
issues.sym: Tapping noise, misfire codes, shaking at idle, or power loss.
issues.why: The deactivating lifters can stick or collapse, sometimes ruining the camshaft.
issues.next: Diagnose quickly to limit engine damage.

issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard and the SUV takes longer to stop. A brake warning may appear.
issues.why: The engine-driven vacuum pump that powers the brake booster can lose output. GM recalled affected V8 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the fix done. A hard pedal deserves immediate attention.

issues.t: 6.2L engine recall for rod and crank defects
issues.sym: Engine knock, low oil pressure, rough running, or a sudden stall.
issues.why: Some engines had defective crankshaft or connecting rod parts that can fail.
issues.next: Check for open recalls. Stop driving if you hear knocking.

issues.t: Heated windshield washer module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: On trucks built with the heated washer fluid option, you may notice a burning smell or smoke from under the hood, or other electrical features acting up. Many owners never see a warning before the module overheats.
issues.why: The small heater that warms the washer fluid can short-circuit internally and overheat. GM recalled it twice and ended up disabling and removing the heater altogether.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the NHTSA recall lookup right away. If the recall is still open, book the free dealer repair now and park outside until it is done. Stop driving and have it towed if you smell burning or see smoke.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling from a cracked condenser
issues.sym: The air conditioning slowly gets weaker and then blows warm, often within the first few years. A shop may find the refrigerant charge is low or empty with no obvious damage.
issues.why: The A/C condenser at the front of the truck, which is built together with a transmission cooler, can crack from repeated heating and cooling and let the refrigerant escape. GM extended coverage on this part for a limited time on certain trucks.
issues.next: Have a shop check the system with leak dye or a sniffer before paying for a simple recharge, since a recharge alone will leak out again. Ask a GMC dealer whether special coverage 17336 ever applied to your VIN.

issues.t: Eight-speed automatic shudder at steady speed
issues.sym: A vibration that feels like driving over rumble strips, usually under light throttle at steady road speeds. It can come and go and may be joined by harsh or clunky shifts.
issues.why: The original transmission fluid in the eight-speed automatic used with the 6.2L engine in these years can take on moisture, which makes the torque converter clutch grab and release unevenly. GM issued a bulletin calling for a full exchange to a revised fluid.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or transmission shop about the fluid exchange in GM bulletin 18-NA-355. Get it done soon, because long-term shudder can wear out the torque converter.

issues.t: Magnetic Ride Control shocks leak or knock
issues.sym: On trucks with the Magnetic Ride Control suspension (standard on Denali), you may see oily fluid on a shock body, hear knocking over bumps, or notice a bouncier ride or a suspension service message.
issues.why: The electronically controlled shocks can develop seal leaks or internal noise as they age. GM has a service bulletin telling dealers how to judge a leak and to replace only the shock that has failed.
issues.next: Have the shocks looked at during your next service. A light film is normal, but fluid running down the shock or a clear change in ride means that shock should be replaced.

issues.t: Ten-speed transmission valve can lock the rear wheels (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden harsh downshift or a brief lockup of the rear wheels while driving, sometimes after a warning message about the transmission. Some owners first notice a rough shift into a lower gear.
issues.why: A control valve inside the ten-speed automatic can wear and lose pressure, which can cause an abrupt downshift that momentarily locks the rear wheels. The 2021 recall covers trucks with the 3.0L diesel, and a later recall covers 2022 trucks. Dealers load software that watches for the fault and limits the transmission before it can lock up.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free software update done promptly. If you feel a harsh downshift or the rear wheels grab, slow down, pull over safely and have the truck towed to a dealer.
